headers.name: base
headers.doc: The base of the Maul RHI API: the library and contract versions, the export and attribute macros, the result codes every fallible function returns, the allocator and the extension chain.

items.name: result
items.doc: The status a fallible function returns. Zero is success, positive values are outcomes that are not errors, negative values are errors. The type has a fixed width so that result structs have one layout in C and C++.

values.name: success
values.doc: The call did what was asked.

values.name: empty
values.doc: There is nothing to return: the notification queue is drained.

values.name: error_invalid
values.doc: An argument is invalid: a null pointer where one is required, a value out of range, a def without its cookie.

values.name: error_capacity
values.doc: A caller buffer, a named limit or the allocator is too small for the result.

values.name: error_stale
values.doc: An id names an object that no longer exists.

values.name: error_unsupported
values.doc: This platform, driver or build cannot do what was asked, or a def carries a critical extension the library does not know.

values.name: error_platform
values.doc: The platform or its GPU driver failed a call the library made.

values.name: error_state
values.doc: The call is not allowed now, in the object's current state.

values.name: error_version
values.doc: The program was built against another contract version.

items.name: version
items.doc: A library version: major, minor and patch.

items.name: allocator
items.doc: The allocator an owner object takes in its def and keeps for its lifetime. Alignment is a power of two. A zeroed allocator means the C library's functions, which serve alignments up to that of max_align_t.

items.name: struct_type
items.doc: The type of a chained struct. Bit 31 clear marks a critical extension, which a library that does not know it refuses; bit 31 set marks a hint it may skip.

values.name: struct_none
values.doc: No struct: never valid in a chain.

values.name: struct_test_driver
values.doc: mrhiTestDriverDef, on an instance def: turns the test driver on.

items.name: chain
items.doc: The header every chained struct opens with. A def's next field, or a chained struct's chain.next, points at the next struct of the chain, or is NULL.

items.name: request_id
items.doc: A request, answered by exactly one notification in its owner's queue.

items.name: get_version
items.doc: Returns the version of the library that was linked, which may differ from the MRHI_VERSION macros a program was compiled with.

returns.doc: The library version.

items.name: result_name
items.doc: Returns the name of a result code, for diagnostics.

returns.doc: A static, NUL-terminated string such as "mrhi_errorCapacity".

args.name: result
args.doc: Any value; an unknown one is named as such.

headers.name: instance
headers.doc: The instance: the root of Maul RHI, made first and destroyed last, which negotiates the contract version and finds the adapters.

items.name: instance
items.doc: An instance, made by mrhiCreateInstance.

items.name: adapter_name_bytes
items.doc: The bytes an adapter's name may take, in UTF-8.

items.name: adapter_id
items.doc: An adapter: a GPU, or a software rasterizer, that a driver found.

items.name: driver_kind
items.doc: The GPU API a driver speaks.

values.name: driver_test
values.doc: The test driver: no GPU, for tests.

values.name: driver_vulkan
values.doc: Vulkan.

values.name: driver_web_gpu
values.doc: The browser's WebGPU.

values.name: driver_metal
values.doc: Metal.

values.name: driver_d3d12
values.doc: Direct3D 12.

items.name: adapter_kind
items.doc: What kind of processor an adapter is.

values.name: adapter_unknown
values.doc: The driver does not say.

values.name: adapter_discrete
values.doc: A GPU with its own memory.

values.name: adapter_integrated
values.doc: A GPU sharing the CPU's memory.

values.name: adapter_virtual
values.doc: A GPU of a virtual machine.

values.name: adapter_software
values.doc: A rasterizer running on the CPU.

items.name: power_preference
items.doc: Which adapters a request prefers.

values.name: power_default
values.doc: The driver's own order.

values.name: power_low
values.doc: Integrated and low-power adapters first.

values.name: power_high
values.doc: Discrete and fast adapters first.

items.name: adapter_info
items.doc: What an adapter is.

members.name: vendor_id
members.doc: The PCI vendor id, or 0 where the platform hides it.

members.name: device_id
members.doc: The PCI device id, or 0 where the platform hides it.

members.name: name
members.doc: The adapter's name in UTF-8, nameLength bytes, not NUL-terminated.

items.name: adapter_request_def
items.doc: Which adapters a request looks for. Build it with mrhiDefaultAdapterRequestDef.

members.name: allow_software
members.doc: Whether software rasterizers may answer.

items.name: instance_notification_kind
items.doc: What an instance notification reports.

values.name: instance_adapters_found
values.doc: An adapter request is answered: its outcome is mrhi_success, and mrhiGetAdapters lists the adapters, or an error.

values.name: instance_device_ready
values.doc: A device finished opening: its outcome is mrhi_success and the device is ready, or an error and the device failed. A device destroyed while opening answers mrhi_errorStale.

items.name: instance_notification
items.doc: A record from an instance's notification queue.

members.name: request_id
members.doc: The request the record answers.

members.name: outcome
members.doc: How the request ended.

items.name: instance_limits
items.doc: The named limits of an instance.

members.name: chain_depth
members.doc: Chained structs one def may carry; 8 by default.

members.name: notifications
members.doc: Records the notification queue holds; 64 by default.

members.name: adapters
members.doc: Adapters the instance keeps; 16 by default.

items.name: instance_def
items.doc: How an instance is made. Build it with mrhiDefaultInstanceDef.

members.name: contract_version
members.doc: MRHI_CONTRACT_VERSION, as the program was built.

items.name: default_instance_def
items.doc: Returns the default instance def: the contract version the program is built against, the C library's allocator and the default limits (8 chained structs per def, 64 notifications, 16 adapters).

returns.doc: The def, with a valid cookie.

items.name: create_instance
items.doc: Makes an instance.

returns.doc: `mrhi_success`; `mrhi_errorInvalid` for a NULL argument, a def without its cookie, a zero limit or an allocator with one function; `mrhi_errorVersion` when the def's contract version is not the library's; `mrhi_errorUnsupported` for a critical extension the library does not know, such as mrhiTestDriverDef in a build without the test driver; `mrhi_errorCapacity` when the chain is deeper than the limit or the allocator fails.

args.name: instance_out
args.doc: Receives the instance; set to NULL on failure.

items.name: destroy_instance
items.doc: Destroys an instance. While any of its devices exists it refuses, counting the call as misuse and destroying nothing.

args.name: instance
args.doc: The instance, or NULL for nothing.

items.name: get_instance_misuse
items.doc: Returns how many calls the instance has refused as invalid input (mrhi_errorInvalid): a count release builds can watch to catch a caller's bugs. Stale ids are not misuse.

returns.doc: The count; 0 for a NULL instance.

items.name: default_adapter_request_def
items.doc: Returns the default adapter request def: the driver's own order, software rasterizers allowed.

returns.doc: The def, with a valid cookie.

items.name: request_adapters
items.doc: Asks the instance's drivers for adapters. The request is answered by one mrhi_instanceAdaptersFound record; until then, mrhiGetAdapters lists the adapters found before.

returns.doc: `mrhi_success` with the request accepted; `mrhi_errorInvalid` for a NULL argument or a def without its cookie; `mrhi_errorUnsupported` for a critical extension the library does not know; `mrhi_errorCapacity` when the notification queue has no room for the answer.

items.name: next_instance_notification
items.doc: Takes the oldest record from the instance's notification queue, first polling its drivers for finished work.

returns.doc: `mrhi_success` with a record; `mrhi_empty` when the queue is drained; `mrhi_errorInvalid` for a NULL argument.

items.name: get_adapters
items.doc: Lists the adapters the last answered request found, best first by its preference.

returns.doc: `mrhi_success`; `mrhi_errorInvalid` for a NULL instance or count, or a NULL array with a capacity.

args.name: adapters
args.doc: Receives up to capacity ids. May be NULL when capacity is 0.

args.name: count_out
args.doc: Receives the number of adapters, which may exceed capacity.

items.name: get_adapter_info
items.doc: Reads what an adapter is.

returns.doc: `mrhi_success`; `mrhi_errorInvalid` for a NULL argument; `mrhi_errorStale` for an adapter the instance no longer has.

items.name: format_caps
items.doc: What a format can do on an adapter. Every adapter meets the floor mrhiFloorFormatCaps would give; the compressed families need their feature.

members.name: sampling
members.doc: Sampled in shaders.

members.name: filtering
members.doc: Sampled with linear filtering.

members.name: rendering
members.doc: A render target.

members.name: blending
members.doc: Blended as a render target.

members.name: storage
members.doc: A storage texture.

members.name: sample_counts
members.doc: The multisample counts as a mask: the bit worth n is set when n samples are supported (1, 2, 4).

vulkan.note: sampleCounts of the format's image properties

items.name: default_limits
items.doc: Returns the floor limits, which every adapter of every driver meets: WebGPU's defaults, 64 root block bytes, no heaps and 2 frames in flight.

returns.doc: The floor.

items.name: get_adapter_features
items.doc: Reads the optional features an adapter can grant.

returns.doc: `mrhi_success`; `mrhi_errorInvalid` for a NULL argument; `mrhi_errorStale` for an adapter the instance no longer has.

items.name: get_adapter_limits
items.doc: Reads the limits an adapter can grant, each at least the floor.

returns.doc: `mrhi_success`; `mrhi_errorInvalid` for a NULL argument; `mrhi_errorStale` for an adapter the instance no longer has.

items.name: get_format_caps
items.doc: Reads what a format can do on an adapter. A compressed format whose feature the adapter lacks can do nothing.

returns.doc: `mrhi_success`; `mrhi_errorInvalid` for a NULL argument or a format the contract does not list; `mrhi_errorStale` for an adapter the instance no longer has.

headers.name: device
headers.doc: The device: the second root of Maul RHI, opened on an adapter with the features and limits a program asks for, and the owner of every GPU object.

items.name: device
items.doc: A device, made by mrhiCreateDevice.

items.name: device_state
items.doc: Where a device is in its life.

values.name: device_opening
values.doc: Made, not yet ready: calls answer mrhi_errorState.

values.name: device_ready
values.doc: Ready for use.

values.name: device_failed
values.doc: Opening failed; only destroying it remains.

values.name: device_lost
values.doc: The GPU or its driver was lost; only destroying it remains.

items.name: device_limits
items.doc: The named limits of a device's own bookkeeping.

members.name: notifications
members.doc: Records the device's notification queue holds; 256 by default.

members.name: samplers
members.doc: Samplers the device holds at once; 256 by default.

members.name: buffers
members.doc: Buffers the device holds at once; 4096 by default.

items.name: device_def
items.doc: How a device is made. Build it with mrhiDefaultDeviceDef and set the adapter.

members.name: adapter
members.doc: The adapter to open, from mrhiGetAdapters.

members.name: features
members.doc: The optional features asked for.

members.name: limits
members.doc: The limits asked for, at least the floor.

items.name: default_device_def
items.doc: Returns the default device def: no adapter, no optional features, the floor limits, 256 notifications, 256 samplers, 4096 buffers and the C library's allocator.

returns.doc: The def, with a valid cookie.

items.name: create_device
items.doc: Makes a device on an adapter. It returns at once with the device opening, and the instance's queue answers the request with mrhi_instanceDeviceReady.

returns.doc: `mrhi_success` with the device opening; `mrhi_errorInvalid` for a NULL argument, a def without its cookie, a zero limit, limits below the floor or an allocator with one function; `mrhi_errorStale` for an adapter the instance no longer has; `mrhi_errorUnsupported` for features or limits beyond the adapter's, or a critical extension the library does not know; `mrhi_errorCapacity` when the instance's queue has no room for the answer or an allocator fails.

args.name: instance
args.doc: The instance that found the adapter.

args.name: device_out
args.doc: Receives the device; set to NULL on failure.

args.name: request_out
args.doc: Receives the id its ready record answers.

items.name: destroy_device
items.doc: Destroys a device in any state. A device still opening answers its request with mrhi_errorStale.

args.name: device
args.doc: The device, or NULL for nothing.

items.name: get_device_state
items.doc: Returns where a device is in its life. Draining the instance's queue is what moves an opening device on.

returns.doc: The state; mrhi_deviceFailed for a NULL device.

items.name: get_device_features
items.doc: Reads the optional features a device was granted.

returns.doc: `mrhi_success`; `mrhi_errorInvalid` for a NULL argument.

items.name: get_device_limits
items.doc: Reads the limits a device was granted.

returns.doc: `mrhi_success`; `mrhi_errorInvalid` for a NULL argument.

items.name: get_device_misuse
items.doc: Returns how many calls the device has refused as invalid input (mrhi_errorInvalid).

returns.doc: The count; 0 for a NULL device.

headers.name: resources
headers.doc: The objects a device owns: samplers, buffers, textures and views, each a generation-checked id.

items.name: filter
items.doc: How texels are filtered.

values.name: filter_nearest
values.doc: The nearest texel.

values.name: filter_linear
values.doc: A weighted average of the nearest texels.

items.name: address_mode
items.doc: How coordinates outside a texture are treated. Clamp to border is absent: WebGPU has no border colors.

values.name: address_clamp_to_edge
values.doc: The edge texel.

values.name: address_repeat
values.doc: The texture repeats.

values.name: address_mirror_repeat
values.doc: The texture repeats, mirrored every other time.

items.name: compare_function
items.doc: A comparison of a new value with a stored one: for comparison samplers, and for depth and stencil tests.

values.name: compare_none
values.doc: No comparison: a plain sampler.

values.name: compare_never
values.doc: Never passes.

values.name: compare_less
values.doc: Passes when less.

values.name: compare_equal
values.doc: Passes when equal.

values.name: compare_less_equal
values.doc: Passes when less or equal.

values.name: compare_greater
values.doc: Passes when greater: reversed-Z depth.

values.name: compare_not_equal
values.doc: Passes when different.

values.name: compare_greater_equal
values.doc: Passes when greater or equal.

values.name: compare_always
values.doc: Always passes.

items.name: sampler_id
items.doc: A sampler of a device.

items.name: sampler_def
items.doc: How a sampler is made. Build it with mrhiDefaultSamplerDef.

members.name: mag_filter
members.doc: Filtering when magnified.

members.name: min_filter
members.doc: Filtering when minified.

members.name: mip_filter
members.doc: Filtering between mip levels.

members.name: lod_min
members.doc: The lowest level of detail sampled, at least 0.

members.name: lod_max
members.doc: The highest level of detail sampled, at least lodMin.

members.name: max_anisotropy
members.doc: 1 to 16; above 1, every filter must be linear.

vulkan.note: maxAnisotropy with samplerAnisotropy, clamped to maxSamplerAnisotropy

members.name: compare
members.doc: A comparison for shadow maps, or mrhi_compareNone.

items.name: default_sampler_def
items.doc: Returns the default sampler def: nearest filtering, clamp to edge, levels of detail 0 to 32, no anisotropy and no comparison.

returns.doc: The def, with a valid cookie.

items.name: create_sampler
items.doc: Makes a sampler on a ready device.

returns.doc: `mrhi_success`; `mrhi_errorInvalid` for a NULL argument, a def without its cookie, a value out of range, anisotropy with a nearest filter, or levels of detail out of order; `mrhi_errorState` for a device that is not ready; `mrhi_errorUnsupported` for a critical extension the library does not know; `mrhi_errorCapacity` when the device's sampler limit is reached.

items.name: destroy_sampler
items.doc: Destroys a sampler. Its id ends at once; the device retires it after the frames that used it.

returns.doc: `mrhi_success`; `mrhi_errorInvalid` for a NULL device; `mrhi_errorStale` for a sampler the device no longer has.

items.name: buffer_usage
items.doc: What a buffer is used for, declared when it is made.

values.name: buffer_vertex
values.doc: Vertex data.

values.name: buffer_index
values.doc: Index data.

values.name: buffer_uniform
values.doc: Uniform data.

values.name: buffer_storage
values.doc: Storage read and written by shaders.

values.name: buffer_indirect
values.doc: Arguments of indirect draws and dispatches.

values.name: buffer_copy_source
values.doc: The source of copies.

values.name: buffer_copy_destination
values.doc: The destination of copies and uploads.

values.name: buffer_query_resolve
values.doc: The destination of query results.

items.name: buffer_id
items.doc: A buffer of a device.

items.name: buffer_def
items.doc: How a buffer is made. Build it with mrhiDefaultBufferDef and set its size and usage. A buffer is never mapped: the frame graph fills and reads it.

members.name: size
members.doc: Bytes, a multiple of 4, at most the device's bufferBytes limit.

members.name: usage
members.doc: Its uses, at least one.

d3d12.note: the resource's flags and the views made of it

items.name: default_buffer_def
items.doc: Returns the default buffer def: no size and no usage, which must be set.

returns.doc: The def, with a valid cookie.

items.name: create_buffer
items.doc: Makes a buffer on a ready device. Its contents are undefined until the frame graph writes them.

returns.doc: `mrhi_success`; `mrhi_errorInvalid` for a NULL argument, a def without its cookie, a size of 0 or not a multiple of 4, or no usage or an unknown one; `mrhi_errorUnsupported` for a size beyond the device's bufferBytes limit or a critical extension the library does not know; `mrhi_errorState` for a device that is not ready; `mrhi_errorCapacity` when the device's buffer limit is reached; `mrhi_errorPlatform` when the driver fails.

items.name: destroy_buffer
items.doc: Destroys a buffer. Its id ends at once; the device retires it after the frames that used it.

returns.doc: `mrhi_success`; `mrhi_errorInvalid` for a NULL device; `mrhi_errorStale` for a buffer the device no longer has.

headers.name: test
headers.doc: The test driver (MAUL_RHI_TEST_DRIVER): a driver without a GPU whose adapters a test describes, for the library's tests and a program's own.

items.name: test_adapter
items.doc: An adapter the test driver finds: its facts, features and limits, and how a device opening on it ends.

members.name: open_outcome
members.doc: The outcome of a device opening on the adapter: mrhi_success, or the error the device fails with.

members.name: limited_format
members.doc: A format the adapter reports limitedCaps for instead of its usual capabilities, to test adapters below the floor; mrhi_formatNone for none.

members.name: objects_before_failure
members.doc: Objects a device on the adapter makes before every further one fails with mrhi_errorPlatform; 0 for no failure.

items.name: test_driver_def
items.doc: Turns the test driver on for an instance, chained on its def with the type mrhi_structTestDriver. The test driver is the only driver of such an instance.

members.name: adapters
members.doc: The adapters the driver finds, in its own order. May be NULL when adapterCount is 0.
